recent.summary: A broad risk-on reversal drove the Nasdaq +1%, led by AI/cloud and crypto-adjacent names surging on two key catalysts: SpaceX confirming no slowdown in AI compute demand and the OCC finalizing GENIUS Act stablecoin rules. Cybersecurity names DDOG (+6.5%) and NET (+5.3%) also spiked on a critical PHP flaw affecting ~70% of websites, while defense (RTX) and healthcare (JNJ) rotated out as geopolitical risk premiums faded on Ukraine peace talk resumption. Open SELL signals on MSTR and PLTR turned deeply painful at -12.2% and -8.4% respectively, with confidence downgraded to LOW as the structural bull catalysts overwhelmed the original theses.

Nasdaq suffered its worst session since June as a chipmaking equipment supply warning crushed semis (AMD -8.1%, INTC -8.0%) and META's AI spending concerns from earnings dragged the broader growth/AI complex below the 50-day moving average. Capital rotated hard into defense and defensives, with LMT surging nearly 7% on a Q3 earnings blowout and an 850-jet F-35 Pentagon deal, while JNJ caught a safe-haven bid as healthcare outperformed. Active signals favor selling AMD and META on multi-source fundamental headwinds, while reaffirming LMT and JNJ buys; AMZN BUY from Tuesday is -4.6% but held as no stock-specific catalyst has emerged.

A sharply bifurcated session saw Energy and Cybersecurity surge — NET +7.29%, SLB +7.08% — driven by Trump's Iran military threat, Gulf undersea cable sabotage risk, and a PHP vulnerability bid, while Big Tech, Financials, and Healthcare sold off on AI spending anxiety and a Dow -650pt macro risk-off move. Open BUY signals on NET (+6.0%), DDOG (+3.6%), and LMT (+2.4%) are all working, but AMZN BUY was closed at -5.5% and flipped to SELL ahead of earnings with Nasdaq below its 50-day. Capital is rotating defensively into infrastructure security and defense as geopolitical escalation enters day 2 and Big Tech earnings risk mounts.

Anthropic's IPO filing rekindled broad AI enthusiasm, lifting semis (INTC +4%, NVDA BUY initiated), cloud, and defense simultaneously while crypto-adjacent names MSTR and META lagged in a risk-on tape. Defense entered day 7 of its rally with LMT +5.1% and RTX +3.4% on sustained Middle East escalation signals (Netanyahu/Iran, Egypt-Saudi/Houthi), prompting a disciplined LMT profit-take after a +7.7% gain from Friday's entry. Mega-cap earnings (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL) loom as the week's binary risk, with META flagged as a live SELL on relative weakness and AMZN held on WATCH pending post-print confirmation.

A broad risk-on rotation drove semiconductors and AI names sharply higher, led by AMD (+5.45%) and AVGO (+4.00%), fueled by Anthropic's IPO S-1 filing confirming massive AI chip demand and a macro tailwind from surging US business equipment spending. Boeing cratered -10.69% on a confirmed Q3 earnings disaster — missed deliveries, slashed production rates — while energy and defense names retreated on Iran diplomacy signals easing geopolitical risk premiums. The week's binary risk events center on MSFT and GOOGL earnings plus the Fed rate decision, with AMZN's AWS read also pivotal for the open SELL position.

ORCL surged +10.7% on blowout earnings and explicit 2030 cash flow guidance, directly countering AI spending fears and sparking a broad risk-on rally in semis and cloud infrastructure (MU +5.86%, AVGO reaffirmed BUY). MSFT's Azure beat after hours provided a second confirming catalyst for AI infra demand, while GOOGL's negative free cash flow and capex blowout dragged Mega-cap Tech sentiment, leaving META as the session's standout laggard (-1.24% on a green tape). Capital rotation is firmly into AI infrastructure and semis, with META and PLTR facing valuation compression and the Fed holding rates at 3.75–4.0% with a hawkish lean adding pressure on rate-sensitive growth names.

Markets split sharply as GOOGL posted its worst single-day drop ever (-12.6%) on structural search revenue fears and AMZN missed profits on soaring AI capex, dragging Big Tech and semis lower. Defense stocks surged for an 8th+ consecutive day led by LHX (+6.84%) on a blowout Q3 with $11B in missile defense awards and FCF +195%, confirming robust DoD spending. Capital rotation out of growth and into defense, healthcare, and consumer staples is accelerating, with active BUY signals on LHX, RTX, and LLY and a high-conviction SELL on GOOGL.

weekly.summary: A BofA AI bubble warning, CoreWeave credit stress, and VIX spiking above 22 triggered a four-session, $260B+ risk-off unwind crushing high-multiple AI, cloud, and crypto names (PLTR, SNOW -8%+, MSTR -9.6% with added MSCI removal headwinds, MARA -9.6%). Capital rotated decisively into Defense (RTX +3.7%, LMT +3.6%) and Energy (CVX +2.6%) on Middle East escalation via Yemen missile strikes and a US SPR solicitation, while AAPL held as the lone resilient core-tech name on iPhone demand, Chinese subsidies, and Berkshire support. Core calls — **BUY RTX, LMT, AAPL; SELL PLTR, MSTR** — remained fully intact across all sessions.

Tech's AI/cloud names (DDOG, AMZN) led an oversold bounce on high-conviction upgrades while defense (NOC blowout earnings, RTX/LMT read-across) and small caps benefited from a broadening rally as geopolitical risk premiums eased on US-Iran and Putin-Trump-Xi diplomacy. AAPL was downgraded to WATCH after a sell-the-news reaction to its foldable launch, crypto-adjacent names (MSTR) remain under SELL pressure despite Bitcoin euphoria, and PLTR's extreme valuation keeps its SELL intact notwithstanding the AI rebound. Key open calls: DDOG and AMZN are high-confidence BUYs, RTX and LMT BUYs supported by NOC's $110B backlog, with MSTR SELL and PLTR SELL both maintained.
